q: After years of rivalry, the two scholars decided to bury the ___.
explain: Bury the hatchet = stop arguing and be friends. Example: The sisters finally buried the hatchet.

notes.grudge: You can hold a grudge, but you bury the hatchet.
notes.daggers: Daggers appear in 'look daggers at', not here.

q: The dragon's offer seemed generous, but there were strings ___.
explain: Strings attached = hidden conditions. Example: a free gift with no strings attached.

q: His story was a ___ herring, designed to distract us.
explain: A red herring = a false clue that distracts. Example: The muddy boots were a red herring.

notes.white: White lie is a different idiom.

q: She has an ___ to grind with the referee; she's never forgiven him.
explain: Have an axe to grind = have a private grievance. Example: He has an axe to grind with the coach.

q: To praise someone so weakly that it sounds like criticism is to ___ them with faint praise.
explain: Damn with faint praise = praise so weakly it sounds like criticism. Example: 'It was... fine' damns it with faint praise.

q: The plan is ___ by a thread; one more setback and it fails.
explain: Hanging by a thread = very close to failing. Example: His hopes were hanging by a thread.

q: Which word means 'deliberately vague to avoid commitment'?
explain: Equivocal = deliberately unclear. Example: an equivocal answer.

notes.unequivocal: Unequivocal is the opposite: totally clear.

q: The prophecy's language was so ___ that only the oldest dragon could interpret it.
explain: Arcane = mysterious, known to few. Example: arcane spells.

q: His speech was full of ___ — pompous words used to sound important.
explain: Grandiloquence = pompous, showy language. Example: The wizard's grandiloquence bored everyone.

notes.understatement: Understatement = saying less than is true.

q: To 'have your cake and eat it' means to ___.
options: be greedy whenever you go to parties
explain: Have your cake and eat it = want two things that can't both happen. Example: You can't skip practice and win; you can't have your cake and eat it.

notes.celebrate a birthday with friends: It isn't about birthdays; it's an idiom.
notes.be greedy whenever you go to parties: It isn't about greed at parties.
notes.share everything fairly with others: Sharing fairly is nearly the opposite.

q: 'The proof of the pudding is in the eating' means ___.
options: you judge something by trying it
desserts are the most important course
cooking well takes years of practice
you should never eat too fast at dinner
explain: You only know if something works by trying it. Example: The new game sounds fun, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating.

q: The scholar's ___ remarks hinted at a deep resentment.
explain: Barbed = sharp and hurtful, with hidden criticism. Example: a barbed joke.

q: To 'steal someone's thunder' means to ___.
options: make a lot of noise in a storm
ruin the weather for their picnic
explain: Steal someone's thunder = take the attention they expected. Example: My brother stole my thunder by announcing his news first.

notes.borrow their ideas without asking: Borrowing ideas is close, but the idiom is about attention.

q: She remained ___ despite the dragon's provocations — utterly calm.
explain: Imperturbable = impossible to upset. Example: an imperturbable goalkeeper.

q: The difference between the two translations is ___, yet it changes the meaning entirely.
explain: Subtle = small and hard to notice. Example: a subtle hint.

notes.blatant: Blatant = very obvious; 'yet' signals a contrast with small.

q: A 'Pyrrhic victory' is one that ___.
options: costs so much it is hardly worth winning
is won very easily against a weak enemy
is won by cheating or breaking the rules
ends a long war that both sides wanted over
explain: A Pyrrhic victory costs so much it's hardly worth it. Example: We won, but lost three players to injury: a Pyrrhic victory.

notes.is won very easily against a weak enemy: An easy win is the opposite.
notes.ends a long war that both sides wanted o: It isn't about ending a war.

q: To 'cut to the chase' means to ___.
explain: Cut to the chase = get to the main point. Example: Cut to the chase: did we win?

notes.edit a film scene: It came from films, but means get to the point.

q: The critic's review was ___: witty, sharp and utterly merciless.
explain: Scathing = severely critical. Example: a scathing review.

q: The scholar's knowledge of medieval poetry is truly ___.
explain: Encyclopaedic = very complete and wide. Example: encyclopaedic knowledge of dinosaurs.

notes.endemic: Endemic = found only in one place.

q: To 'bite the bullet' means to ___.
options: refuse to talk about a problem
explain: Bite the bullet = face something unpleasant bravely. Example: I bit the bullet and went to the dentist.

notes.refuse to talk about a problem: Refusing to talk is avoiding, the opposite.

q: Her ___ manner concealed a fierce ambition.
explain: Self-effacing = modest, not drawing attention. Example: a self-effacing champion.

notes.self-serving: Self-serving = only helping yourself, not hiding ambition.

q: The two theories are not mutually ___; both may be true.
explain: Mutually exclusive = can't both be true. Example: Fast and careful aren't mutually exclusive.

q: The team captain was accused of ___, saying one thing and doing another.
explain: Hypocrisy = saying one thing and doing another. Example: It's hypocrisy to preach and not practise.

notes.hypothesis: A hypothesis is an idea to test.

q: A 'Herculean' task is one that ___.
explain: Herculean = needing enormous effort (from Hercules). Example: Tidying my room was a Herculean task.

q: The tale was a ___ of truth and invention, impossible to untangle.
explain: Melange = a mixture. Example: a melange of flavours.

q: He tends to ___ on trivial details, missing the bigger picture.
explain: Fixate (verb) on = focus too much on. Example: Don't fixate on one mistake.

q: 'To be on tenterhooks' means to be ___.
explain: On tenterhooks = nervously waiting. Example: We were on tenterhooks waiting for the results.

q: The dragon's reply was ___, revealing nothing.
explain: Inscrutable = impossible to read or understand. Example: an inscrutable smile.

q: To 'pass the buck' means to ___.
explain: Pass the buck = push responsibility onto someone else. Example: Don't pass the buck; own the mistake.

notes.move quickly past a problem: It isn't about moving past problems.

q: The prize is awarded for ___ achievement in literature.
explain: Outstanding = excellent. Example: outstanding work.

notes.standing out: Standing out is a verb phrase, not an adjective before a noun.

q: Her apology was ___, as everyone knew she didn't mean it.
explain: Perfunctory = done without real feeling. Example: a perfunctory 'sorry'.

q: The fox's ___ plan to steal the cheese fooled every crow in the forest.
explain: Cunning = clever at tricking others. Example: a cunning trick.

q: The ___ young knight had never held a sword before.
explain: Callow = young and inexperienced. Example: a callow recruit.

q: The ___ old oak had stood in the schoolyard for three hundred years.
explain: Venerable = respected because of age or wisdom. Example: a venerable professor.

q: Baby turtles are extremely ___ as they crawl towards the sea.
explain: Vulnerable = easily harmed. Example: vulnerable to attack.

notes.invincible: Invincible = impossible to defeat, the opposite.

q: The guards remained ___ all night, watching for the dragon.
explain: Vigilant = carefully watching for danger. Example: Stay vigilant.

q: She was ___ in her refusal: absolutely no pets in the library!
explain: Vehement = showing very strong feeling. Example: a vehement denial.

q: The professor's instructions were so ___ that nobody knew what to do.
explain: Nebulous = vague and unclear. Example: a nebulous idea.

q: His answer was ___: three words that said everything.
explain: Laconic = using very few words. Example: a laconic reply.

q: The ___ parrot never stopped chattering, even at night.
explain: Loquacious = very talkative. Example: a loquacious guide.

q: The ___ lighthouse keeper rarely spoke to visitors.
explain: Taciturn = habitually quiet. Example: a taciturn farmer.

notes.garrulous: Garrulous = talking too much about unimportant things.

q: Dolphins are ___ animals that live in large, playful groups.
explain: Gregarious = liking company. Example: a gregarious host.

q: The ___ inventor hadn't left his workshop in years.
explain: Reclusive = avoiding contact with others. Example: a reclusive author.

q: The peacock looked ___ in its shimmering feathers.
explain: Resplendent = splendidly colourful. Example: resplendent in gold.

q: With a calculator, learning the times tables isn't ___: you still need them!
explain: Redundant = no longer needed or useful. Example: The old machine became redundant.

notes.relevant: Relevant would mean connected, which reverses the point.

q: The troll's table manners were utterly ___.
explain: Uncouth = rude and lacking good manners. Example: uncouth behaviour.

q: The robot had an ___ ability to guess what we were thinking.
explain: Uncanny = strange in a way that's hard to explain. Example: an uncanny resemblance.

q: After a week in the forest, the explorers looked ___.
explain: Unkempt = untidy, messy (hair, appearance). Example: unkempt hair.

q: The squirrel was an ___ accomplice: it carried the key away without knowing.
explain: Unwitting = not aware of what you are doing. Example: an unwitting helper.

q: The archer's aim was ___: every arrow hit the centre.
explain: Unerring = always accurate. Example: an unerring instinct.

q: The ___ puppies knocked over every potted plant.
explain: Unruly = difficult to control. Example: an unruly class.

q: Despite her fame, the astronaut was modest and ___.
explain: Unassuming = modest, not wanting attention. Example: an unassuming hero.

q: The dragon's ___ golden throne was covered in jewels.
explain: Ostentatious = designed to impress or show off. Example: an ostentatious car.

q: The monks lived in ___ rooms with only a bed and a candle.
explain: Austere = very plain, without comfort. Example: an austere lifestyle.

q: Squirrels are ___: they store food for the winter.
explain: Provident = careful to plan for the future. Example: a provident saver.

q: Agatha Christie was a ___ writer, with over sixty novels.
explain: Prolific = producing a great amount. Example: a prolific inventor.

notes.prodigious: Prodigious = remarkably impressive or large, not about quantity of works.

q: Mozart showed ___ talent as a young child.
explain: Prodigious = remarkably impressive. Example: a prodigious memory.

q: The ending of the fairy tale was rather ___: no magic, no surprise.
explain: Prosaic = ordinary and unimaginative. Example: a prosaic explanation.

q: The magician tried to ___ the audience with smoke and mirrors.
explain: Beguile = charm or trick. Example: beguiled by her smile.

q: The coach ___ the team for not taking the match seriously.
explain: Berate = scold angrily. Example: She berated him for being late.

q: The old wizard ___ his spellbook to his favourite apprentice.
explain: Bequeath = pass on after death, or hand down. Example: She bequeathed her house to the school.

q: Older kids sometimes ___ the ideas of younger ones, which isn't fair.
explain: Belittle = make something seem unimportant. Example: Don't belittle her achievement.

q: The kind words ___ her confidence before the audition.
explain: Bolster = support or strengthen. Example: bolster morale.

q: Constant teasing can ___ a child's self-belief.
explain: Undermine = gradually weaken. Example: Lack of sleep undermines your health.

notes.understate: Understate = make seem smaller than it is.

q: Careful research ___ every claim in her science report.
explain: Underpin = support or form the basis of. Example: Trust underpins friendship.

q: The heavy snow ___ our school trip, cutting it to one day.
explain: Curtail = cut short or reduce. Example: Rain curtailed the match.

q: Two witnesses ___ the girl's story about the glowing fox.
explain: Corroborate = confirm with evidence. Example: The video corroborated his account.

q: He ___ an elaborate excuse involving aliens and a lost bus.
explain: Concoct = invent a story, or mix a dish. Example: concoct a plan.

q: The teacher ___ the phone until the end of the day.
explain: Confiscate = take away officially. Example: The guard confiscated the sword.

q: The elders ___ a meeting under the great tree.
explain: Convene = call people together for a meeting. Example: convene a council.

notes.conversed: Conversed = talked, and isn't used with a meeting as object.

q: Her face ___ more than words ever could.
explain: Convey = communicate. Example: Music conveys emotion.

notes.conferred: Conferred = gave an honour, or discussed.

q: The queen ___ a knighthood on the brave baker.
explain: Confer (on) = give an honour. Example: The title was conferred on her.

q: The rumour about the haunted lab ___ through the school in minutes.
explain: Permeate = spread through every part. Example: The smell permeated the house.

q: She ___ the ancient map, searching for hidden symbols.
explain: Peruse = read carefully. Example: peruse the menu.

notes.persevered: Persevered = kept trying; it needs with or in.

q: The final riddle ___ even the cleverest apprentices.
explain: Perplex = completely confuse. Example: The question perplexed me.

notes.persisted: Persisted = continued; it doesn't take an object.

q: Old cartoons can ___ silly stereotypes about scientists.
explain: Perpetuate = make something (often bad) continue. Example: perpetuate a myth.

q: The dragon gave a ___ of contentment as it curled up by the fire.
explain: A sigh can express relief or contentment. Example: a sigh of relief.

notes.gasp: A gasp is a sudden breath of surprise.
notes.groan: A groan expresses pain or annoyance.
notes.wail: A wail is a long cry of grief.

q: The crowd ___ in surprise as the rabbit vanished.
explain: Gasp = take a sudden breath in surprise. Example: She gasped in horror.

notes.snorted: Snorted = made a rude nose sound.

q: The kitten ___ at the bright, flashing toy.
explain: Gaze = look steadily for a long time. Example: gaze at the stars.

notes.peeked through: Peek through needs something to look through.

q: I only ___ the shooting star before it disappeared.
explain: Glimpse = see for a very short time. Example: I glimpsed a fox.

notes.gazed: Gazed = looked for a long time.
notes.stared: Stared = looked fixedly for a long time.

q: The judges ___ every detail of the sandcastle.
explain: Scrutinise = examine very carefully. Example: scrutinise the evidence.

q: The tiny stream ___ through the meadow.
explain: Meander = wind slowly. Example: a meandering path.

q: The runaway cart ___ down the hill.
explain: Hurtle = move very fast, out of control. Example: The rock hurtled towards us.

notes.sauntered: Sauntered = walked in a relaxed way.

q: The cat ___ across the garden as if it owned the place.
explain: Saunter = walk slowly and confidently. Example: He sauntered in late.

notes.scurried: Scurried = ran with quick small steps, nervously.

q: The mice ___ into their holes when the cat appeared.
explain: Scurry = move quickly with small steps. Example: Ants scurried everywhere.

q: The giant ___ through the forest, crushing bushes.
explain: Lumber = move heavily and awkwardly. Example: The bear lumbered off.

q: Sorting the library's million books is no ___ in the park.
explain: No walk in the park = not easy. Example: Training for a marathon is no walk in the park.

notes.picnic: No picnic is a different idiom with the same meaning, but not 'in the park'.

q: Don't put all your eggs in one ___: enter more than one competition.
explain: Don't put all your eggs in one basket = don't risk everything on one thing. Example: Apply to several schools; don't put all your eggs in one basket.

notes.box: Box isn't used in this idiom.
notes.nest: Nest isn't used in this idiom.
notes.bag: Bag isn't used in this idiom.

q: The inventor was ahead of her ___: nobody understood her machine.
explain: Ahead of your time = with ideas too modern for your era. Example: Da Vinci was ahead of his time.

q: When the dragon smiled, the knight smelled a ___.
explain: Smell a rat = suspect a trick. Example: When he offered free sweets, I smelled a rat.

notes.mouse: Mouse isn't used in this idiom.
notes.skunk: Skunk isn't used in this idiom.
notes.fox: Fox isn't used in this idiom.

q: The apprentice was left holding the ___ when the others ran away.
explain: Left holding the baby = left with responsibility for a problem. Example: They left me holding the baby.

notes.bag: Holding the bag is the American version; this is the British idiom.
notes.book: Book isn't used in this idiom.
notes.candle: Candle is in 'can't hold a candle to', a different idiom.

q: The new robot can't hold a ___ to the old one.
explain: Can't hold a candle to = is much worse than. Example: The sequel can't hold a candle to the original.

notes.torch: Torch is in 'carry a torch for', a different idiom.
notes.light: Light isn't used in this idiom.
notes.lamp: Lamp isn't used in this idiom.

q: Her prize-winning story was a ___ above the rest.
explain: A cut above = clearly better. Example: This café is a cut above the others.

notes.slice: Slice isn't used in this idiom.
notes.notch up: Notch up = achieve; 'a notch above' exists, but not 'a notch up above'.

q: The mystery was finally solved, and the penny ___.
explain: The penny dropped = someone finally understood. Example: After a minute, the penny dropped.

q: You can't judge a book by its ___.
explain: Don't judge a book by its cover = don't judge by appearances. Example: The shy boy turned out to be hilarious.

q: The two scholars don't see eye to ___ on anything.
explain: See eye to eye = agree. Example: We don't always see eye to eye.

notes.face: Face isn't used in this idiom.
notes.nose: Nose isn't used in this idiom.
notes.ear: Ear isn't used in this idiom.

q: After the argument, there was some bad ___ between the two teams.
explain: Bad blood = lasting dislike between people. Example: There's bad blood between the clubs.

notes.feeling to: Bad feeling exists, but not 'bad feeling to'.

q: The detective decided to play it by ___ and see what happened.
explain: Play it by ear = decide as you go. Example: We'll play it by ear.

notes.eye: Eye isn't used in this idiom.
notes.heart: Heart isn't used in this idiom.
notes.hand: Hand isn't used in this idiom.

q: The robot's answer was so long-winded; I wish it would get to the ___.
explain: Get to the point = say the important thing. Example: Please get to the point.

notes.end: Get to the end means finish, not focus.
notes.bottom of: Get to the bottom of = find the truth.

q: We need to get to the ___ of this mystery.
explain: Get to the bottom of = discover the real cause. Example: We'll get to the bottom of this.

notes.base: Base isn't used in this idiom.
notes.root of: The of is already there, so root of repeats it.
notes.floor: Floor isn't used in this idiom.

q: Our science project is still up in the ___: we haven't chosen a topic.
explain: Up in the air = undecided. Example: Our plans are up in the air.

notes.sky: Sky isn't used in this idiom.
notes.clouds: Clouds is in 'head in the clouds', a different idiom.
notes.wind: Wind isn't used in this idiom.

q: The dreamy inventor always had her head in the ___.
explain: Head in the clouds = not paying attention to real life. Example: Stop daydreaming; get your head out of the clouds.

notes.air: Up in the air means undecided, a different idiom.
notes.stars: Stars isn't used in this idiom.
notes.sky: Sky isn't used in this idiom.

q: Finishing the quest in one night was a tall ___.
explain: A tall order = a very difficult request. Example: Winning every game is a tall order.

q: The scholars argued until the ___ came home.
explain: Until the cows come home = for a very long time. Example: You can argue until the cows come home.

notes.sheep: Sheep isn't used in this idiom.
notes.birds: Birds isn't used in this idiom.
notes.horses: Horses isn't used in this idiom.

q: The village library is in a ___ state after the storm.
explain: A parlous state = a dangerously bad condition (formal). Example: The roof is in a parlous state.

notes.pernicious: Pernicious = harmful in a slow, hidden way.

q: Too much screen time can have a ___ effect on sleep.
explain: Pernicious = harmful, often gradually. Example: a pernicious habit.

notes.parlous: Parlous = in a bad state, used with 'state'.

q: Clear skies made it a ___ night for stargazing.
explain: Propitious = favourable. Example: a propitious moment.

q: The ___ seven-year-old was already doing algebra.
explain: Precocious = developed earlier than usual. Example: a precocious talent.

q: The stack of books was balanced in a very ___ position.
explain: Precarious = unstable, likely to fall. Example: a precarious ledge.

q: The idea that the moon is made of cheese is ___.
explain: Preposterous = absurd, ridiculous. Example: a preposterous excuse.

q: She has a ___ memory for dates and names.
explain: A prodigious memory = an amazingly good one. Example: prodigious strength.

q: After ___ negotiations, the cats and dogs agreed to share the garden.
explain: Protracted = lasting longer than expected. Example: a protracted illness.

q: The witch gave a ___ laugh that echoed through the tower.
explain: Sinister = suggesting evil. Example: a sinister smile.

q: The snake moved with ___ grace through the grass.
explain: Sinuous = curving and graceful. Example: the sinuous river.

q: The robot's speech sounded ___ and unnatural.
explain: Stilted = stiff and awkward. Example: a stilted conversation.

q: Her ___ in the face of the storm inspired the whole crew.
explain: Equanimity = calmness under pressure. Example: She accepted the news with equanimity.

notes.equator: Equator = the line around Earth's middle.

q: The ___ of the ancient manuscript was questioned by experts.
explain: Authentic → authenticity (being real). Example: the authenticity of the painting.

q: The two stories have a striking ___ to each other.
explain: Resemblance to = similarity. Example: a strong resemblance to her mother.

notes.semblance: Semblance = an outward appearance, often false.

q: There was no ___ of order in the dragon's cave.
explain: A semblance of = a small amount or appearance of. Example: a semblance of normality.

q: The fairy's ___ made her the best negotiator in the kingdom.
explain: Diplomacy = skill in dealing with people sensitively. Example: She handled it with diplomacy.

q: The magician's ___ of hand amazed everyone.
explain: Sleight of hand = skilful, quick hand tricks. Example: a card trick done by sleight of hand.

notes.slight: Slight = small; it sounds the same but is spelled differently.
notes.sleigh: Sleigh = a sledge pulled by animals.

q: Ignoring the warning was the ___ of foolishness.
explain: The height of + noun = the most extreme example. Example: the height of rudeness.

q: The wizard spoke with such ___ that the class hung on every word.
explain: Eloquent → eloquence (noun). Example: She argued with great eloquence.

notes.elocution of: Elocution of needs a noun after it.

q: The penguins showed remarkable ___ in surviving the blizzard.
explain: Fortitude = courage in pain or difficulty. Example: She bore the pain with fortitude.
